faqs.q: Do I need to file ITR if my income is below the taxable limit?
faqs.a: It is generally not compulsory if your income is below the basic exemption limit and no other legal condition requires you to file. Filing anyway is still useful, because it lets you claim a refund of any TDS deducted, carry forward losses and show proof of income for loans, credit cards and visas.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss the ITR filing deadline?
faqs.a: You can usually still file a belated return by 31 December of the assessment year, unless the government extends it. A late fee of up to Rs 5,000 applies, capped at Rs 1,000 if your total income is Rs 5 lakh or less, along with interest on any unpaid tax, and you lose the right to carry forward most losses.

faqs.q: Which ITR form should a salaried person file?
faqs.a: Most resident salaried individuals with total income up to Rs 50 lakh, from salary, one house property and other sources such as interest, can use ITR-1 (Sahaj). If you have income above that, more than one house property, or capital gains not allowed in ITR-1, you generally need ITR-2. The portal also helps you pick the right form.

faqs.q: How do I e-verify my ITR, and what if I don't?
faqs.a: You can e-verify your return using an Aadhaar OTP, net banking, an electronic verification code through your bank or demat account, or a digital signature certificate. A return that is not verified within the allowed time is treated as incomplete and will not be processed, so any refund will also be held up.
